extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent practitioners (patent owners and third-party reexamination requesters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for filing, conducting, and evaluating ex parte reexamination proceedings of patents, including what prior art and submissions may be considered, claim treatment, and compliance with statutes and regulations (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 112, 305; 37 CFR provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excused delay in patent owner response
rubrics_metrics.description: The delay in filing such response may be excused if it is shown to the satisfaction of the Director that the delay was unavoidable (petition under § 1.137(a)); or the response may nevertheless be accepted if the delay was unintentional (petition under § 1.137(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to accept an unavoidably delayed response must comply with § 1.137(a); a petition to accept an unintentionally delayed response must comply with § 1.137(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirement for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party in the reexamination proceeding in the manner provided by § 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document must reflect service or the document may be refused consideration by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of third-party active participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535, and no further submissions on behalf of the reexamination requester will be acknowledged or considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further submissions on behalf of any third parties will be acknowledged or considered only if: (1) in accordance with § 1.510 or § 1.535; or (2) entered in the patent file prior to the date of the order for ex parte reexamination pursuant to § 1.525.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of third-party submissions filed after order
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions by third parties, filed after the date of the order for ex parte reexamination pursuant to § 1.525, must meet the requirements of and will be treated in accordance with § 1.501(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions after the order are governed by § 1.501(a) and may be excluded if not compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fees for reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.20(c)(6), except for specific listed petition types (e.g., extension of response period under paragraph (c), petitions under paragraph (e) to accept delayed response, petitions under § 1.78 to accept unintentionally delayed benefit claim, and petitions under § 1.530(l) for correction of inventorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check § 1.20(c)(6) and enumerated exceptions before filing a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding is ex parte despite third-party request
rubrics_metrics.description: Once ex parte reexamination is ordered pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 304 and the times for submitting any responses to the order have expired, no further active participation by a third party reexamination requester is allowed, and no third party submissions will be acknowledged or considered unless they are in accordance with 37 CFR 1.510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination proceedings will be ex parte, even if ordered based on a request filed by a third party, because this was the intention of the legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner cannot file third-party-prepared papers for requester
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may not file papers on behalf of the requester and thereby circumvent the intent of the ex parte reexamination legislation and the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers prepared by a third party and filed by the patent owner will not be entered; the entire submission will be returned. See Emerson Elec. Co. v. Davoil, Inc., and MPEP §§ 2266 and 2267.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination authorities and special dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination will be conducted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104, 1.105, 1.110-1.113, and 1.116 (35 U.S.C. 132 and 133) and will result in issuance of a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570. The proceeding shall be conducted with special dispatch pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full search will not routinely be made by the examiner; reexamination proceeds even if copy of order is returned undelivered because notice under 37 CFR 1.11(c) is constructive notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who conducts the reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination will ordinarily be conducted by the same patent examiner who made the decision on whether the reexamination request should be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.515(c) is granted, the reexamination will normally be conducted by another examiner (see MPEP § 2248).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of prior art to be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to discussion below, the examiner must also consider patents and printed publications: (A) cited by another reexamination requester under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.915; (B) cited in a patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or a requester’s reply under 37 CFR 1.535 if they comply with 37 CFR 1.98; (C) cited by the patent owner under a duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.555) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.98; (D) discovered by the examiner in searching; (E) of record in the patent file from earlier examination; and (F) of record in the patent file from any 37 CFR 1.501 submission prior to date of an order if it complies with 37 CFR 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where items are submitted by a party in compliance with rules, degree of consideration is normally limited by the degree to which filer explained content and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of consideration tied to explanation of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: When patents, publications, and other items are submitted by a party in compliance with the rules, the requisite degree of consideration to be given to such information will normally be limited by the degree to which the party filing the information citation has explained the content and relevance of the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner initials adjacent to citations do not signify that the information has been considered further than so indicated in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required for submitted references (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2) requires a legible copy of: (1) each foreign patent; (2) each publication or that portion which caused it to be listed, other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office; (3) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims, and any drawing of the application, or that portion of the application which caused it to be listed; (4) all other information or that portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to supply the required legible copies can limit consideration; parties should submit only the portion that caused listing when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: No submission of copies of copending reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not required nor is it permitted that parties submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings and applications (which copies can be mistaken for a new request/filing); rather, submitters may provide the application/proceeding number and its status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A submission that is not permitted entry will be returned, expunged, or discarded at the sole discretion of the Office. The exception to 37 CFR 1.98(d)(1) does not apply to reexamination proceedings since a reexamination proceeding does not receive 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit from the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-NIRC submissions by patent owner require petition and explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the NIRC has been mailed, when the patent owner provides a submission of patents and printed publications, or other information described in 37 CFR 1.98(a), after the NIRC has been mailed, the submission must be accompanied by (A) a factual accounting providing a sufficient explanation of why the information submitted could not have been submitted earlier, and (B) an explanation of the relevance of the information submitted with respect to the claimed invention in the reexamination proceeding. This is provided via a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 (with petition fee) for entry and consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements facilitate the Office’s compliance with special dispatch; both items (A) and (B) must be satisfied to justify interrupting the proceeding after the NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission during printing cycle requires stronger showing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission of patents and printed publications, or other information described in 37 CFR 1.98(a), is made while a proceeding is in its printing cycle, the patent owner must provide an unequivocal statement as to why the art submitted makes at least one claim unpatentable, an amendment to such claim or claims, and an explanation as to how the amendment causes such claim or claims to be patentable, in addition to the factual accounting why it could not have been submitted earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 (with petition fee) for withdrawal of the reexamination proceeding from the printing cycle; a grantable petition must provide the requisite showing discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions after order not considered unless part of request or reply
rubrics_metrics.description: No consideration will be given to a third party requester submission of patents and printed publications, or other information, that is filed in the reexamination proceeding unless it is part of the request for reexamination or the requester’s reply under 37 CFR 1.540.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party attempts to add art after order outside the permitted mechanisms will be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of prior art on official forms and printing on certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination request must provide a listing of the patents and printed publications as provided for in 37 CFR 1.98. The examiner must list on a form PTO-892, PTO/SB/08A or 08B, or PTO/SB/42 (or equivalent) all prior art patents or printed publications which have been cited in the decision on the request, applied in making rejections or cited as being pertinent during the reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All citations listed on form PTO-892 and all citations not lined-through on any form PTO/SB/08A or 08B, or PTO/SB/42 will be printed on the reexamination certificate under 'References Cited.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions entitling a submission to entry and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission of patents and/or publications is entitled to entry and citation in the reexamination certificate when it complies with 37 CFR 1.98 and is submitted: (A) by the patent owner in the statement under 37 CFR 1.530; (B) by the reexamination requester in the reply under 37 CFR 1.535; (C) prior to the order of reexamination under 37 CFR 1.501 by any party; and/or (D) by the patent owner under the duty of disclosure requirements of 37 CFR 1.555.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions meet 37 CFR 1.98 and are submitted via the authorised procedural vehicle to be entered and cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination — patents/printed publications and 35 U.S.C.112
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.552(a): Claims in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted in the reexamination proceeding, on the basis of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination focuses on patents and printed publications; 35 U.S.C. 112 issues are limited to new/amendatory subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims may not enlarge scope of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.552(b): Claims in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will not be permitted to enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new or amended claims are examined to ensure that the scope of the original patent claims is not enlarged (see 35 U.S.C. 305).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination does not resolve issues beyond patents/publications and enlargement
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.552(c): Issues other than those indicated in paragraphs (a) and (b) (i.e., patents/printed publications and enlargement) will not be resolved in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other issues are raised by parties, examiner will note existence of such issues in next Office action and patent owner may consider filing a reissue application to have them considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent-owner statements to construe claims after order
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.552(d): Any statement of the patent owner and any accompanying information submitted pursuant to § 1.501(a)(2) which is of record in the patent being reexamined may be used after a reexamination proceeding has been ordered to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim when applying patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent-owner statements cannot be used at the initial order stage to establish a substantial new question but can be used in examination to determine claim meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art rejections limited to patents and printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections on prior art in reexamination proceedings may only be made on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections cannot be based on matters other than patents or printed publications (e.g., public use or sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, conduct issues), even if relying on a patent or printed publication as support; prior art must be applied under appropriate portions of 35 U.S.C. 102 and/or 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening patents/printed publications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections may be made in reexamination proceedings based on intervening patents or printed publications where the patent claims under reexamination are entitled only to the filing date of the patent and are not supported by an earlier foreign or United States patent application whose filing date is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include situations involving 35 U.S.C. 120 effective dates; see In re Ruscetta and In re van Langenhoven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting can be basis for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue of double patenting is appropriate for consideration in reexamination, both as a basis for ordering reexamination and during subsequent examination on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should determine whether double patenting raises a substantial new question at the request stage and whether a rejection based on double patenting is appropriate in examination (see In re Lonardo and MPEP §§ 804-804.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations only explain prior art patents/publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations or other written evidence which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications in more detail may be considered in reexamination, but any rejection must be based upon the prior art patents or printed publications as explained by the affidavits or declarations or other written evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections cannot be based on affidavits/declarations alone; they must rely on patents/printed publications (as explained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions used only in combination with patents/printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission, per se, may not be the basis for establishing a substantial new question of patentability, but an admission by the patent owner of record in the file or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written statements submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) if relied upon in the request must be explained per 37 CFR 1.510(b)(2) showing how each patent owner claim scope statement is used to determine proper meaning of a claim in connection with prior art applied to that claim; admissions can be used in examination to interpret or modify prior art; third parties may not submit admissions made outside the file or court record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation rule in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: During reexamination, claims are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification and limitations in the specification are not read into the claims (In re Yamamoto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For expired patents, claim construction pursuant to Phillips (ordinary and customary meaning as understood by a person of ordinary skill at time of invention) should be applied since expired claims are not subject to amendment. The statutory presumption of validity (35 U.S.C. 282) has no application in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112 issues limited to new/amendatory matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new claims are presented or where any part of the disclosure is amended, the claims in the reexamination proceeding are to be examined for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112. Consideration of 35 U.S.C. 112 issues should, however, be limited to the amendatory (e.g., new language) matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A term in an original patent claim cannot be examined as too broad in a new or amended claim unless the amendatory matter creates the issue. Rewriting a dependent claim as independent cannot be examined under 112 unless the rewriting raises a new question (e.g., lack of antecedent). See MPEP § 2163 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on adding new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 305 provides for examination under 35 U.S.C. 132, which prohibits the introduction of new matter into the disclosure. Thus, the question of new matter should be considered in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where new matter is added to the claims or affects claim limitations, the claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, for failing to meet the written description requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the specification may raise 112 issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the specification is amended in a reexamination proceeding, the examiner should make certain that the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112 are met. An amendment to the specification can redefine the scope of the terms in a claim such that the claim is no longer clear or is not supported by the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment to the specification can result in failure of the claims to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112 even where the claims are not amended in any respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must not enlarge scope of patent (restatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in the proceeding must not enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with 37 CFR 1.552(b) and 35 U.S.C. 305; ensure any new/amended claim is not broader than original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of prior art consideration dependent on record availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree of consideration of information from the patent file and its parent files is dependent on the availability of the information (e.g., if a reference other than a U.S. patent is not scanned into the Image File Wrapper, what was said about that reference in the patent’s record is the full extent of consideration unless parties appropriately supplied a copy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should supply copies where the office record lacks the full reference to ensure adequate consideration.
